question.text: LTCG on UNLISTED shares (held > 24 months) post July 2024:

explanation.text: The Logic: Unlisted shares held for more than 24 months are long-term capital assets. As part of the July 2024 Budget's rationalisation of capital-gains taxation, LTCG on such unlisted shares is taxed at a flat 12.5%, and the earlier benefit of indexation on the cost of acquisition for this asset class was withdrawn. The Trap: '20%' was the pre-rationalisation rate; '20% with indexation' was the pre-July-2024 combination that has been replaced; 'No tax' is clearly incorrect — unlisted-share LTCG is fully taxable. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook (pp. 185-186) supports that unlisted shares held more than 24 months are long-term capital assets, but does not state the 12.5% unlisted-share LTCG rate or the removal of indexation in the pages checked. The framing above is based on the post-July-2024 Income Tax Act provisions rather than a workbook quote.
